# Hypothesis: zero -> C if same color appears on both sides in same row OR same col (any distance), else 2

                L=[cc for cc in range(c) if i[r][cc]!=0]; R=[cc for cc in range(c+1,w) if i[r][cc]!=0]

                elif U and D and i[U[-1]][c]==i[D[0]][c]: v=i[U[-1]][c]
                out[r][c]=v if v is not None else 2
    return out

from collections import Counter as C
def f(i):
    H,W=len(i),len(i[0])
    bg=C(v for r in i for v in r).most_common(1)[0][0]
    res=[[bg]*W for _ in range(H)]
    for r in range(H):
        for c in range(W):
            if i[r][c]!=bg: continue
            lo=[k for k in range(c) if i[r][k]!=bg]; hi=[k for k in range(c+1,W) if i[r][k]!=bg]
            U=[k for k in range(r) if i[k][c]!=bg]; D=[k for k in range(r+1,H) if i[k][c]!=bg]
            def hrow(a,b): return a and b and i[r][a-1]==i[r][b] and all(i[r][k]==bg for k in range(a,b))
            def vcol(a,b): return a and b and i[a-1][c]==i[b][c] and all(i[k][c]==bg for k in range(a,b))
            h=hrow(lo[-1],hi[0]) if lo and hi else False
            v=vcol(U[-1],D[0]) if U and D else False
            if h or v: res[r][c]= i[r][lo[-1]] if h else i[U[-1]][c]; continue
            sides=[]
            if lo and hi: sides.append((i[r][lo[-1]],i[r][hi[0]]))
            if U and D: sides.append((i[U[-1]][c],i[D[0]][c]))
            if len(sides)>=2:
                # same color on opposite pair -> fill with that color
                pairs=[t for t in sides if t[0]==t[1]]
                if pairs: res[r][c]=pairs[0][0]; continue
                # also mixed-but-each-side has own marker? fallback: use pair colors if any
                res[r][c]=sides[0][0]
            elif sides: res[r][c]=sides[0][0]
            else: res[r][c]=2
    return res
for name in ['Demo pair 1','Demo pair 2','Demo pair 3','Demo pair 4']:
    i,o=G[name+' input'],G[name+' output']
    p=f(i)
    mis=[(r,c,p[r][c],o[r][c]) for r in range(len(o)) for c in range(len(o[0])) if p[r][c]!=o[r][c]]
    print(name,'nbad',len(mis),mis[:10])

from collections import Counter as C, deque
def ray(i,r,c,dr,dc,bg):
    rr,cc=r+dr,c+dc
    while 0<=rr<len(i) and 0<=cc<len(i[0]) and i[rr][cc]==bg: rr+=dr; cc+=dc
    return (i[rr][cc], rr-r, cc-c) if (0<=rr<len(i) and 0<=cc<len(i[0])) else None
def f(i):
    H,W=len(i),len(i[0])
    bg=C(x for r in i for x in r).most_common(1)[0][0]
    res=[[i[r][c] if i[r][c]!=bg else 2 for c in range(W)] for r in range(H)]
    for r in range(H):
        for c in range(W):
            if i[r][c]!=bg: continue
            L=ray(i,r,c,0,-1,bg); R=ray(i,r,c,0,1,bg)
            U=ray(i,r,c,-1,0,bg); D=ray(i,r,c,1,0,bg)
            # candidate: markers on opposite sides with PURE bg gap and same color
            cand=None
            if L and R and L[0]==R[0] and L[0]!=bg and all(i[r][k]==bg for k in range(c-L[1]-1, c+1)): cand=L[0]
            elif U and D and U[0]==D[0] and U[0]!=bg and all(i[k][c]==bg for k in range(r-U[1]-1, r+1)): cand=U[0]
            if cand is not None: res[r][c]=cand
    return res

from collections import Counter as C, deque
def f(i):
    H,W=len(i),len(i[0])
    cnt=C(v for r in range(H) for c in range(W) for v in [i[r][c]]).most_common()
    bg=[v for v,_ in cnt if _==max(cnt,key=lambda kv:kv[1])[1]][0]
    res=[[2]*W for _ in range(H)]
    seen=[[False]*W for _ in range(H)]
    for start_r,start_c in [(r,c) for r in range(H) for c in range(W)]:
        if i[start_r][start_c]!=bg or seen[start_r][start_c]: continue
        comp=[]; q=deque([(start_r,start_c)]); seen[start_r][start_c]=True
        while q:
            a,b=q.popleft(); comp.append((a,b))
            for dr,dc in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                aa,bb=a+dr,b+dc
                if 0<=aa<H and 0<=bb<W and i[aa][bb]==bg and not seen[aa][bb]:
                    seen[aa][bb]=True; q.append((aa,bb))
        if len(comp)<3: continue
        touches=any(r in (0,H-1) or c in (0,W-1) for r,c in comp)
        if touches: continue
        # fill with surrounding fg color
        colset=C(i[a][b] for a,b in comp).pop() if False else None
        # determine enclosing color: neighbors of comp cells
        neigh=C()
        for a,b in comp:
            for dr,dc in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                aa,bb=a+dr,b+dc
                if 0<=aa<H and 0<=bb<W and i[aa][bb]!=bg:
                    neigh[i[aa][bb]]=neigh.get(i[aa][bb],0)+1
        main=neigh.most_common(1)[0][0]
        for a,b in comp: res[a][b]=main
    # fg cells: keep
    return [[i[r][c] if i[r][c]!=bg else res[r][c] for c in range(W)] for r in range(H)]

import numpy as np, os,glob,re
from collections import Counter
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    G={}
    for f in sorted(glob.glob(d+'/../../sessions/*.jsonl')):
        t=open(f).read().replace('\\n','\n')
        for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair (\d+) (input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
            kk=m[1]; h,w=int(m[4]),int(m[5])
            rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
            if all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows) and kk not in G:
                G[kk]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load()
# what determines output bg color? check mapping of which color became 2 (the minority new color) vs others
for i in range(1,9):
    a=np.array(G[f'Demo pair {i} input']); b=np.array(G[f'Demo pair {i} output'])
    H,W=a.shape
    # find cells whose value changed
    ch=[(r,c,int(a[r][c]),int(b[r][c])) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if a[r][c]!=b[r][c]]
    print(i, 'bgA',Counter([int(x) for x in a.flatten()]).most_common(), 'changes:',sorted(set((u,v) for _,_,u,v in ch)))

import numpy as np
from collections import Counter
def norm(cells):
    r0=min(p for p,_ in cells); c0=min(q for _,q in cells)
    return frozenset((p-r0,q-c0) for p,q in cells), (r0,c0)
for i in [5,6,7,8]:
    A=np.array(G[f'Demo pair {i} input']); B=np.array(G[f'Demo pair {i} output'])
    bgA=Counter([x for row in A for x in row]).most_common(1)[0][0]
    bgB=Counter([x for row in B for x in row]).most_common(1)[0][0]
    objs=[(v,cs) for v,n,cs in comps(A,bgA)]
    objsets=[(frozenset(cs),v) for v,cs in [(o[1],o[2]) for o in comps(A,bgA)]]
    # brute force: assign each out cell to an in-object translation; check consistency
    print('=== pair',i,'bgA',bgA,'bgB',bgB)
    # try: each object translated so its norm cells map onto B cells with same relative offsets, all cells covered once
    def try_assign(objs,Bcells):
        B=set(Bcells)
        n=len(objs); res=[]
        # greedy assignment via bipartite matching over possible translations
        import itertools
        trans=[]
        for v,cells in objs:
            nrm,(r0,c0)=norm(cells)
            H=max(p for p,_ in nrm)+1; W=max(q for _,q in nrm)+1
            poss=[]
            for dr in range(-H,B.shape[0]):
                for dc in range(-W,B.shape[1]):
                    cov=sum(1 for p,q in nrm if 0<=p+dr<B.shape[0] and 0<=q+dc<B.shape[1] and (p+dr,q+dc) in B)
                    poss.append((cov,(dr,dc)))
            trans.append(poss)
        # solve exact cover: product search pruned
        best=None
        import sys
        sys.setrecursionlimit(10000)
        def solve(k,covered,cur):
            nonlocal best
            if best is not None and len(cur)==n: return
            if k==n:
                if covered==len(B) and len(set().union(*[set(cur[j][1] and [] for j in range(n))])==0): pass
                return
            if covered+len(trans[k][0][0])<len(B): return
            for c,(dr,dc) in enumerate(trans[k]):

import numpy as np, json
from collections import Counter
G=load()
def solve_pair(i):
    A=np.array(G[f'Demo pair {i} input']); B=np.array(G[f'Demo pair {i} output'])
    bgA=Counter([x for row in A for x in row]).most_common(1)[0][0]
    bgB=Counter([x for row in B for x in row]).most_common(1)[0][0]
    objs=[(v,set(cs)) for v,cs in comps(A,bgA)]
    Bset={(r,c) for r in range(B.shape[0]) for c in range(B.shape[1]) if B[r][c]!=bgB}
    n=len(objs); sols=[]
    def solve(k,covered,acc):
        nonlocal sols
        if len(sols)>8: return
        if covered==Bset and k==n:
            sols.append(tuple(acc)); return
        if k==n: return
        cells=objs[k][1]; H=max(p for p,_ in cells)+1; W=max(q for _,q in cells)+1
        cands=[]
        for dr in range(-H,B.shape[0]):
            for dc in range(-W,B.shape[1]):
                new={(p+dr,q+dc) for p,q in cells}
                if new<=Bset and new and not(new&covered):
                    cands.append((new,dr,dc,objs[k][0]))
        cands.sort(key=lambda t:len(t[0]))
        for new,dr,dc,v in cands:
            acc.append((v,dr,dc,new)); solve(k+1,covered|new,acc); acc.pop()
    solve(0,set(),[])
    return sols
# check colors match B: does each object keep its own color? verify with solution
for i in range(1,9):
    sols=solve_pair(i)
    A=np.array(G[f'Demo pair {i} input']); B=np.array(G[f'Demo pair {i} output'])
    ok=True
    for v,dr,dc,new in sols[0]:
        allsame=all(B[p]==v for p in new)
        if not allsame: ok=False
    print(i,'unique color per object:',ok, 'colors:',{v for v,_,_,_ in sols[0]})

from collections import Counter
def ruleR(g):
    H=len(g); W=len(g[0])
    c=Counter(x for r in g for x in r); maj=c.most_common(1)[0][0]

            v=g[y][x]
            if v!=maj: row.append(v); continue
            Rs={g[y][t] for t in range(W) if g[y][t]!=maj}
            Cs={g[t][x] for t in range(H) if g[t][x]!=maj}
            S=Rs|Cs
            row.append(next(iter(S)) if len(S)==1 else 2)

from collections import Counter
import json
G=load()
def f(g):
    H=len(g); W=len(g[0])
    c=Counter(v for r in g for v in r); maj=c.most_common(1)[0][0]
    out=[]
    for y in range(H):
        row=[]
        for x in range(W):
            v=g[y][x]
            if v!=maj: row.append(v); continue
            R=[g[y][t] for t in range(W) if g[y][t]!=maj]; C=[g[t][x] for t in range(H) if g[t][x]!=maj]
            sR,sC=set(R),set(C)
            if not sR and not sC: row.append(maj); continue
            if sR and sC and sR.isdisjoint(sC): row.append(2); continue
            if sR and sC: row.append(next(iter(sR&sC))); continue
            row.append(next(iter(sR if sR else sC)))
        out.append(row)
    return out
allok=True
for i in range(1,9):
    a=f(G[f'Demo pair {i} input']); b=G[f'Demo pair {i} output']
    d=sum(1 for y in range(len(a)) for x in range(len(a[0])) if a[y][x]!=b[y][x]); allok&=d==0
    print(i,'mismatch' if d else 'ok',d)
print('ALL OK' if allok else 'MISMATCH')
print(json.dumps(f(G['Test input'])))
